messages:
emma_marketing: @kai_runtime quick ask for the launch: we need a benchmark pack that highlights behavior under infrequent, bursty user traffic (not just steady-state). Can eng/runtime produce raw artifacts + a 1-slide summary by Friday EOD?

emma_marketing: Must-haves: P95/P99 tail during bursts, coldstart latency curve after long idle, tokens/sec during brief spikes, and cost-per-1M-tokens across hosted/dedicated/quantized. Also one short blurb on batching/warmup tradeoffs for the blog.

kai_runtime: Clarify: what arrival patterns count as "bursty/sparse"? models/variants? regions? KV cache behavior? deadline strict?

emma_marketing: Arrival patterns: 1) Poisson baseline (med), 2) repeated 60s bursts after 10m idle (x5), 3) single 2-min spike after 60m idle. Models: flagship float32, int8 quantized, and the distilled small. Region: primary us-west1, single sanity run eu-west1. KV: persist within bursts, flush after idle to exercise coldstart.

toni_analytics: From analytics: export tokenization.csv (tokens per prompt), raw timing traces, and 20 paired outputs per token bucket (float vs quant) for quality checks. We'll compute ROUGE/len-delta ourselves.

jules_infra: We can attach perf traces. Enabling GPU telemetry (pci stats) adds ~10% overhead. Want it?

emma_marketing: Not needed for slides unless trivial. Keep overhead low.

kai_runtime: Plan: concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16,32], token buckets small(1-16)/med(40-120)/large(400-800) with 50/35/15 split, greedy decoding for latency, seed=314159 for determinism. Measurement: 30s ramp, then 5m steady-state per point. Batching configs: off and burst-tuned small-window. Sound good?

emma_marketing: Yes. Include exact run-config.json and CLI commands so marketing can reproduce smoke checks. Also include sample payloads (3 per bucket) and naming scheme for artifacts.

kai_runtime: We'll lock tokenizer to "v2-bytepair" and note tokenizer version in metadata. Artifact path pattern: s3://redwood-bench/launch/3109876543/{variant}/{arrival}/{run-id}/. We'll provide presigned links.

toni_analytics: Also include a 50-sample outputs tarball per variant if feasible, and a small CSV listing token counts and basic quality deltas for paired examples.

jules_infra: Scheduling ETA: smoke bundle in ~6h, full sweep + artifacts in ~28-36h depending on queue. Trace IDs attached to each run.
\enkai_not_real: (typo)

bench-bot: bench-run-3109876600 scheduled by kai_runtime  variants: float32|quantized|distilled; arrivals: poisson|repeated-burst|single-spike; concurrency: [1,4,8,16,32]; batching: off|burst-tuned; region: us-west1.

kai_runtime: We'll produce: CSVs with P50/P95/P99 (request/token), throughput vs concurrency curves, coldstart heatmap (time-since-idle vs latency), run-config.json, tokenization.csv, outputs.tar.gz (paired examples), and a 1-slide markdown summary with headline P95 and cost-per-1M-tokens.

emma_marketing: For the headline, call out the variant with the best latency vs cost tradeoff and a plain-English note on how often P99 exceeds our reliability target during bursts. We'll edit wording.

toni_analytics: Note: quantized runs sometimes change token counts if tokenizer diverges; please include token-level diffs and lock tokenizer version.

kai_runtime: Locked to v2-bytepair. We'll tag runs with seed and tokenizer_version. If quantized outputs show drift we'll include 20 hand-picked paired examples in human-readable form.

jules_infra: If you want per-token flamegraphs, ask now. They take extra collector CPU and add overhead.

emma_marketing: Skip flamegraphs for now. Only include if they do not delay ETA.

kai_runtime: Understood. ETA for full artifact bundle ~30h. If marketing needs faster: we can push a minimal smoke pack in ~6h and follow up with the full sweep.

emma_marketing: 30h is fine. Ping #marketing if anything blocks. Thanks team :rocket:
